p: White City holds a special place in Puttshack's history: the first venue opened here at Westfield London in 2018. The company was founded by the brothers behind Topgolf, who set out to give mini golf the same high-tech makeover. The key is what they call Trackaball technology, which tracks every putt and scores it automatically, so the courses can react to each shot and nobody has to keep count.

A few tips for your round. Spend a minute on the first hole getting used to how the screens and scoring work. Take your time on the trickier holes; rushing usually ends in a bounce off the wrong wall. Swap who goes first each hole so it stays fair, and keep an eye on the group behind so you don't hold things up.

For a group outing, book well ahead, particularly for weekend evenings and the festive season. Arrive a little before your tee time to grab drinks and get settled. If you're planning food too, decide whether you'll eat before, during or after the round so you're not caught out by a hungry group halfway through.

While you're nearby, Wormwood Scrubs, a big sweep of open space, is a short trip north for a breather. Back at Westfield, there's a cinema and lots of places to eat, so you can easily stretch a round of mini golf into a full day or evening out.
